explanations: luna: The source-section root غ ش و is used in the verse's covering of sight, a direct transfer of the night-cover image to perception. | terra: The section carries night's covering into the inward life as a veil over perception; this ayah places غِشَاوَةٌ over the unbelievers' eyes after heart and hearing are sealed.
terra: The section carries the root of fashioning between soul and sky; this ayah turns to the heaven and fashions its seven heavens with سَوَّىٰهُنَّ.

luna: The cloud is made a shade over the people; it gives a Quranic cloud-cover scene that parallels the source section's secondary cloud image over the sun. | terra: The section's secondary عقر image is a cloud covering the sun's eye; this ayah does not mention the sun, so the protective counterimage supplied by its shading cloud remains tentative.

terra: The section follows the root ف ج ر from dawn's splitting to moral rupture; this ayah uses the root for the rock bursting into twelve springs, an opening that gives measured provision rather than destroying a veil.
terra: The section treats succession of night and day as an ordered sign; this ayah likewise names their alternation among concrete signs for people who reason.

luna: The white thread of dawn becomes distinct from the black thread of night; this makes the section's light breaking through darkness a visible boundary. | terra: The section defines fajr as light splitting night's blackness; this ayah makes the white thread of dawn distinguishable from the black thread of night.

luna: God brings night into day and day into night; the reciprocal entrance states the section's exchange of cover and light. | terra: The section shows night and day repeatedly taking over one visible field; this ayah expresses the same boundary as God inserting night into day and day into night.
terra: The section moves the sky's revealed and darkened face into the moral life; this ayah contrasts faces whitened with faces blackened on the Day of judgment.

luna: The alternation of night and day is named among the signs for people of understanding, sharing the section's invitation to notice the ordered sky. | terra: The section's sky scene makes the night-day relay perceptible as created order; this ayah points to the creation of heavens and earth and the alternation of night and day as signs.

terra: The section joins shameful concealment with pushing a daughter or soul into earth; this ayah shows Cain learning from a raven how to cover his brother's corpse, distinguishing burial of the dead from concealment that destroys the living.
terra: The section moves a covering from the sky to blocked inward perception; this ayah places coverings over hearts and heaviness in ears so that hearers do not understand the signs.

terra: The section's night covers a field in which successive lights appear; this ayah begins Abraham's observed sequence when night covers him and a star becomes visible, before moon and sun in 6:77-78.
terra: The section makes the moon a follower within a changing celestial order; this ayah contributes the moon's rising and setting between the star of 6:76 and the sun of 6:78.

terra: The section distinguishes the sun as the great visible source while insisting that celestial bodies pass through an order; this ayah contributes the sun's rising and setting and Abraham's refusal to treat a setting body as Lord.

luna: “فَالِقُ الْإِصْبَاحِ” names God as splitter of daybreak, then joins night as repose and sun and moon as reckoning; it gathers the section's dawn, cover, and measured motion. | terra: The section's dawn splits night's blackness while night, sun, and moon keep measure; this ayah joins فَالِقُ ٱلْإِصْبَاحِ, night as repose, and sun and moon as calculation in one scene.
terra: The section maps the opened and covered sky onto the soul; this ayah contrasts one given reviving light to walk among people with one trapped in darknesses.

terra: The section contrasts a protective covering with fujūr's tearing of it; after Adam and his wife disobey, this ayah has their nakedness appear and makes them patch garden leaves over themselves.

luna: The verse distinguishes ordinary clothing from “لِبَاسُ التَّقْوَىٰ”; that protective-garment metaphor directly develops the source-section root و ق ي as guarding cover. | terra: The section explains taqwā through a thin protective cloth and distinguishes protective covering from concealment; this ayah explicitly names لِبَاسُ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ, the garment of taqwā, as the better clothing.
terra: The section's moral rupture removes a protective veil; this ayah warns that Satan stripped the first parents' clothing in order to show them their nakedness.
terra: The section defines punishment as a covering laid over a people; this ayah gives Hell's inhabitants a bed below and غَوَاشٍ, coverings of fire, above.

luna: The source-section root غ ش و appears in the night covering day, while day pursues it quickly; the image makes the alternation an active chase. | terra: The section defines غ ش و as covering and turns the night-day relay into pursuit; this ayah has God cover day with night as it pursues swiftly and subjects sun and moon.

luna: The she-camel is given as a sign and protected from harm; this supplies the fuller scene behind the section's Thamud ending. | terra: The section calls Thamud's she-camel an eye-opening sign; this ayah presents her as a clear sign from their Lord and commands the people not to harm her.

luna: Thamud hamstring the she-camel; the source-section's root ع ق ر for cutting the camel is used in this parallel account. | terra: The section names عقر as the crime that precedes the covering punishment; this ayah repeats that Thamud hamstrung the she-camel and defied their messenger.

luna: The quake seizes Thamud after they kill the camel, giving a direct account of the covering destruction associated with the section's final scene. | terra: The section's دمدمة means eradication closing over the offenders; after the hamstringing in 7:77, this ayah has the earthquake leave them fallen lifeless in their homes.

luna: The verse names ḍuḥā as a time when punishment may come while people play; it puts the section's open daylight beside danger rather than safety. | terra: The section associates ضُحَىٰ with open daylight but غاشية with enclosing punishment; this ayah warns that punishment may instead arrive at forenoon while a town plays, a specific reversal of darkness as punishment's setting.
terra: The section joins taqwā to the fate awaiting a soul or people; this ayah tells the oppressed believers that the earth is God's and the final outcome is for the muttaqīn.
terra: The section uses ج ل و for a created thing becoming manifest; this ayah uses تَجَلَّىٰ for the Lord's manifestation to the mountain, whose crushing marks the limit of ordinary disclosure.
luna: The root ف ج ر also describes springs bursting from rock; this concrete opening sense echoes the source-section's dawn breaking through darkness and fujur tearing a covering.

terra: The section distinguishes protective covering from punishment that closes over people; this ayah suspends the mountain over Israel like a canopy they think is about to fall, making a shelter-form into a threat.
terra: The section distinguishes a protective cover from a destructive one; this ayah has God cover the believers with drowsiness as security before battle.
luna: The verse pairs cleansing with “تُزَكِّيهِمْ”; it makes explicit the purification sense that the section gives to the source-section root ز ك و.

luna: The verse distinguishes the sun as “ضِيَاءً” and moon as “نُورًا” and gives the moon phases for reckoning, clarifying the two lights and measured sequence. | terra: The section distinguishes the sun as a radiating source from the moon that follows in measured stages; this ayah calls the sun radiance, the moon light, and assigns the moon phases for reckoning time.
terra: The section follows measured changes across one celestial face; this ayah names the alternation of night and day and what God created in the heavens and earth as signs.
luna: The rewarded faces in this verse are free of dust and humiliation, the luminous opposite of faces covered with pieces of night in 10:27.
luna: Evil faces are as if covered with dark pieces of night (“قِطَعًا مِنَ اللَّيْلِ مُظْلِمًا”); this makes the section's night-cover into a moral image.

luna: The verse pairs a restful night with a day made “مُبْصِرًا,” stating the same concealment/visibility boundary in human terms. | terra: The section contrasts night's cover with day's visible spread; this ayah makes night for rest and day مُبْصِرًا, sight-giving.

luna: People fold their breasts and cover themselves with garments to hide; the shared غ ش و covering root extends the section's outside cover to inward concealment. | terra: The section carries physical covering into inward concealment; this ayah depicts people folding themselves and covering with clothes while God knows both what they hide and disclose.
terra: The section defines تلا as coming after and following; this ayah uses the same direct sense when a witness from God follows an earlier proof.

luna: The she-camel has a share of water and the people a known day's share; this develops the watering arrangement surrounding the section's camel scene. | terra: The section contrasts an opened sign with chosen blindness; this ayah calls the she-camel God's sign and warns Thamud not to touch her with harm.

luna: After the warning, they hamstring the camel; this parallels the source-section root ع ق ر and connects it to the announced consequence. | terra: The section's fatal action is the hamstringing of the camel; this ayah repeats فَعَقَرُوهَا and gives the perpetrators a final three-day interval.

luna: The cry seizes the wrongdoers after the camel is hamstrung, describing the punishment that follows the same offense. | terra: The section's punishment closes over the people after their crime; this ayah completes the 11:65 account with the blast leaving the wrongdoers lifeless in their dwellings.
luna: The next verse says they were as if they had never lived there; it completes 11:67's destruction with the disappearance that the section links to annihilation.

luna: The verse says the self inclines toward evil except where God shows mercy; it makes the section's fujur within the nafs a concrete moral tendency, without erasing the stated counterforce of taqwa.

luna: The verse warns of a “غَاشِيَةٌ” from God's punishment; the section's covering root thus names a threat that can overtake a people. | terra: The section develops غَاشِيَة as punishment that covers a whole people; this ayah asks whether an enveloping punishment from God may come upon those who feel secure.
luna: The sun and moon each run to an appointed term beneath the raised heavens, giving the section's recurring heavenly order a measured frame.

luna: The earth is spread (“مَدَّ الْأَرْضَ”), a specific parallel to the section's spread-earth image in the whole surah. | terra: The section's night covers day through غ ش و; this ayah repeats that exact cosmic operation after describing the earth spread out beneath the sky.
terra: The section moves the sky's concealment and disclosure into human inward life; this ayah equates hidden and spoken words, then contrasts one concealed by night with one going openly by day.
terra: The section hears alternating succession in the family of عُقْبَىٰ; this ayah uses مُعَقِّبَاتٌ for successive guardians before and behind a person, adding protection to following.
terra: The section links protective taqwā to what follows a person's choices; this ayah names Paradise as عُقْبَى ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوا۟ and contrasts it with the unbelievers' end.

luna: Sun and moon are kept in continuous service, alongside night and day; the verse gathers the same four-part cosmic order. | terra: The section's sun, moon, night, and day form a tireless order; this ayah names all four as continually subjected for human benefit.
terra: The section develops punishment as a covering and repeatedly treats a visible face as the surface covered; this ayah says fire تَغْشَىٰ the offenders' faces over garments of pitch.
terra: The section includes the earth's spreading as part of the same created order as sun and moon; this ayah says God extended the earth and set firm mountains in it.
terra: The section hears celestial breathing around the fashioned soul; this ayah directly joins God's fashioning the human, سَوَّيْتُهُ, to breathing spirit into him.

luna: Night, day, sun, and moon are all subjugated for people; the verse gathers the same celestial actors into one ordered scene. | terra: The section reads the four opening oath-objects as one governed system; this ayah gathers night, day, sun, moon, and stars under God's command.

luna: The preceding verse describes a father's face darkening at news of a daughter; it supplies the shame that leads into the hiding and burial alternatives in 16:59. | terra: The section explicitly introduces the father of 16:59 through his darkened face; this ayah shows his face turning black before he hides himself and contemplates burial.

luna: The verse says the father may hide the girl in the dust (“يَدُسُّهُ فِي التُّرَابِ”); it is the section's direct Quranic scene for the source-section's root د س و as hiding and burying. | terra: The section explains دَسَّىٰهَا through hiding oneself and pushing another into earth; this ayah unites both acts as the father hides from his people and considers يَدُسُّهُۥ فِى ٱلتُّرَابِ.

luna: The verse says garments protect from heat and violence (“تَقِيكُمُ”); this is a Quranic concrete use of the source-section root و ق ي for protective covering. | terra: The section grounds و ق ي in material coverings that protect; this ayah says God made garments تَقِيكُمُ ٱلْحَرَّ and armor that protects in battle.

luna: Night and day are signs: the night sign is blotted and the day sign made “مُبْصِرَةً”; this makes concealment and visibility explicit and ties them to reckoning. | terra: The section stages night as covering and day as making visible; this ayah effaces the sign of night and makes the sign of day مُبْصِرَةً so people can seek provision and count time.
terra: The section's inward cover prevents disclosed truth from being received; this ayah places coverings over hearts and heaviness in ears while the Quran is recited.

luna: God gave Thamud the she-camel as a seeing sign (“مُبْصِرَةً”); it directly matches the section's visible sign and their response to it. | terra: The section contrasts a sign that opens eyes with the blindness Thamud chooses; this ayah calls the she-camel مُبْصِرَةً and says Thamud wronged her.
luna: The root ف ج ر describes making a spring burst from the earth; the shared opening/gushing sense connects the section's dawn split with a different concrete image.

terra: The section joins the sun's movement, open exposure, and protective concealment; this ayah describes sunlight inclining away from the cave at rising and setting while its sleepers remain in an open space within it.
terra: The section links concealment of the soul to veiled perception; this ayah says persistent rejecters have coverings placed over their hearts and heaviness in their ears.
terra: The section links ضحى with open exposure and distinguishes coverings; this ayah finds a people at sunrise for whom no سِتْرًا against the sun had been made.
terra: The section records ضحى as open, visible standing; Moses fixes the public gathering with Pharaoh for ضُحًى, when the assembled people can witness it openly.
terra: The section uses covering for an annihilating punishment; this ayah says the sea covered Pharaoh's people with what covered them, the same emphatic pattern heard in 53:54.
terra: The section records the secondary sense of standing exposed in the sun; this ayah promises Adam that in the Garden he will not تَضْحَىٰ, suffer uncovered solar exposure.
terra: The section says fujūr tears the protecting curtain; this ayah repeats the enacted pattern as Adam's disobedience exposes the couple's nakedness and they begin covering it with leaves.
terra: The section sets protective taqwā against the soul's ruin and closes on consequence; this ayah states that the final outcome, ٱلْعَاقِبَةُ, belongs to taqwā.

luna: The verse names night, day, sun, and moon together, with each swimming in an orbit; it is a compact parallel to the section's ordered celestial scene. | terra: The section insists that none of the four actors breaks sequence; this ayah names night, day, sun, and moon together and says each swims in an orbit.
terra: The section turns celestial seeing and covering into moral sight and blindness; this ayah says the truly blind organs are the hearts within breasts, not the eyes.

luna: The verse again describes night entering day and day entering night, joining the alternation to God's rule over creation. | terra: The section's ordered covering and disclosure is a continuous exchange; this ayah repeats the mutual entry of night and day as evidence of divine power.
terra: The section hears alternation inside its vocabulary of following; this ayah attributes the recurrent اختلاف of night and day to God.

luna: The verse says God purifies whom He wills; it grounds the section's purification image in divine agency rather than self-assertion. | terra: The section attributes success to purification of the soul; this ayah marks the boundary of human agency by saying none would be purified without God's grace and that God purifies whom He wills.

luna: The verse layers wave, wave, and cloud over darkness in the deep sea; it supplies a specific layered obscuration that extends the section's covered-light image without claiming it depicts a sun-obscuring cloud. | terra: The section develops covering as layered darkness; this ayah stages a deep sea covered by wave above wave and cloud above them, darknesses in which one scarcely sees a hand.

terra: The section's عقر branch imagines cloud covering the sun's eye; this ayah shows clouds amassed under divine direction while their lightning nearly takes eyesight, and 24:44 then turns night and day.

luna: God alternates night and day, and the verse calls this a lesson for those who see; it makes the section's repeated transition perceptible as a sign. | terra: The section presents night and day as taking turns over one field; this ayah says God turns night and day about and calls that a lesson for those with sight.
luna: The verse depicts an extended shadow, making the sun its guide; this connects the source section's revealing daylight to the changing visibility of what the light reaches.
luna: The shadow is drawn in gradually as the sun rises over it; this gives a measured example of light changing what is covered.

luna: Night is made a “لِبَاسًا” and day a rising; the clothing image makes the section's night-cover and daylight-openness concrete. | terra: The section distinguishes orderly and protective covering from destructive concealment; this ayah makes night a garment, sleep repose, and day a renewed arising.

luna: The verse calls the sun a “سِرَاجًا” and the moon “مُنِيرًا”; their paired illumination echoes the section's sun-source and moon-following scene. | terra: The section's sun is a radiating source and its moon a distinct follower; this ayah places an illuminating moon beside a blazing lamp in the constellated sky.

luna: Night and day are made “خِلْفَةً,” each succeeding the other; this gives the section's closing succession a direct formulation. | terra: The section hears succession in عُقْبَىٰ and in the moon following the sun; this ayah makes night and day خِلْفَةً, replacements for one another for remembrance and gratitude.
luna: The she-camel and people have their allotted drinking days; this is a close parallel to the camel's provision and turn in the surah's full context.
luna: The people are warned not to touch the camel with harm; this states the boundary whose violation leads to the section's final destruction scene.

luna: They hamstring the camel, matching the source-section root ع ق ر for the act that triggers the punishment. | terra: The section anchors the fall of Thamud in عقر; this ayah again says they hamstrung the she-camel and immediately became regretful.

luna: The punishment seizes them after the hamstringing, directly completing the same offense-to-destruction sequence. | terra: The section's دمدمة is the collective consequence of the camel's killing; this ayah completes 26:157 by saying the punishment seized them.

terra: The section asks the reader to see how a rejected sign ends in a punishment that closes over its people; this ayah explicitly commands looking at the outcome of Thamud's plot and says all were destroyed.
terra: The section's annihilation leaves nothing standing; this ayah points to Thamud's houses lying ruined because of their wrongdoing.
terra: The section opposes destructive fujūr to protective taqwā; beside Thamud's ruined houses, this ayah says God saved those who believed and had taqwā.

luna: Night is made for rest and day “مُبْصِرًا”; the pair directly expresses the section's covering and seeing roles. | terra: The section's night and day have opposed but coordinated functions; this ayah again makes night a dwelling of rest and day sight-giving.

luna: The hypothetical unending night asks who could bring light; it marks the boundary that makes the section's night/day succession a divine provision. | terra: The section's light depends on an ordered succession rather than an independent possession; this ayah asks who could bring light if God made night permanent.

luna: The hypothetical unending day asks who could bring night for rest; it states the reverse limit to the section's day/night cycle. | terra: The section also needs covering night, not endless exposure; this ayah asks who could bring a night of rest if God made day permanent.

luna: The verse says God made night and day from mercy so people can rest and seek bounty; it states the complementary roles staged in the section. | terra: The section treats disclosure and covering as two fitting parts of one order; this ayah names night for rest and day for seeking bounty as a mercy.
terra: The section closes the soul's choice upon its consequence; this ayah says the final outcome, ٱلْعَاقِبَةُ, is for those who avoid exaltation and corruption, the people of taqwā.

terra: The section says Thamud received an eye-opening sign yet preferred blindness; this ayah points to their visible dwellings and says Satan turned them from the path although they possessed sight.

luna: The punishment “يَغْشَاهُم” from above and below; the source-section's covering action becomes an engulfing judgment. | terra: The section's غاشية is a punishment enveloping a people; this ayah depicts punishment covering the wrongdoers from above and from beneath their feet.

luna: Sleep at night and seeking bounty by day are signs; this gives a human response to the same alternation of concealment and light. | terra: The section gives night and day distinct but coordinated effects; this ayah places human sleep by night and day beside seeking God's bounty within the same pair of signs.
luna: Giving zakat for God's face is described as being multiplied; it supports the source-section's secondary growth sense of the purification root.

luna: Night enters day and day enters night, while sun and moon each run to a term; this combines the section's changing light with measured celestial motion. | terra: The section combines the night-day relay with the governed motions of sun and moon; this ayah joins mutual entry of night and day to both bodies running to a named term.
terra: The section uses covering both for ordered night and destructive enclosure; this ayah has waves cover people like canopies until they call God sincerely.
terra: The section lets the fashioned soul carry the sky's breathing imagery; this ayah joins سَوَّىٰهُ, fashioning the human, with breathing spirit into him.

terra: The section defines protection through a woman's inner cloth between cloak and hair; this ayah commands women to draw their outer garments close so they may be recognized and protected from harm.

luna: The verse says God makes night enter day and day enter night and subjugates sun and moon, a direct counterpart to the section's ordered succession. | terra: The section's sequence is measured and finite; this ayah again joins the interpenetration of night and day to the sun and moon running for an appointed term.
terra: The section opposes making the soul grow to hiding it; this ayah says whoever purifies does so for his own soul, making the action reflexive and its benefit personal.
terra: The section joins covering with loss of perception; this ayah says فَأَغْشَيْنَاهُمْ so that the enclosed people cannot see.
terra: The section distinguishes life-giving dawn rupture from destructive moral rupture; this ayah uses the same root for springs opened among gardens, showing a fruitful physical splitting.

luna: The sign is night, from which day is stripped (“نَسْلَخُ مِنْهُ النَّهَارَ”), a direct image of one light giving way to another. | terra: The section makes daylight disclose and night cover one face; this ayah reverses the viewpoint, stripping day from night so that people suddenly stand in darkness.

luna: The sun runs to its appointed course (“تَجْرِي لِمُسْتَقَرٍّ لَهَا”), adding motion and measure to the section's ordered celestial scene. | terra: The section presents the sun as a source moving through a measured order; this ayah gives the sun its appointed course and limit.

luna: The moon is assigned phases (“مَنَازِلَ”), a concrete account of the moon's changing position in the same ordered sky. | terra: The section's following moon is understood through ordered stages; this ayah assigns the moon measured phases, preparing the non-overtaking rule in 36:40.

luna: The verse says the sun does not catch the moon and night does not precede day; this gives the section's following and succession a fixed order. | terra: The section's moon follows the sun without taking its place; this ayah says neither sun can overtake moon nor night outstrip day, placing that following inside an inviolable celestial order.
terra: The section places فُجُور and تَقْوَى as opposed possibilities within the soul; this ayah asks whether the muttaqīn could be treated like the fujjār.
terra: The section carries completion and breath from the sky into the soul; this ayah repeats the conjunction of fashioning the human and breathing spirit into him.

luna: God “يُكَوِّرُ” night over day and day over night, then the sun and moon each run to a term; the wrapping image directly parallels the section's exchanged light and cover. | terra: The section's single face is alternately covered and disclosed in an ordered relay; this ayah wraps night over day and day over night while sun and moon each run to a fixed term.
terra: The section distinguishes protective تقوى from harmful coverings; this ayah surrounds people with layers of fire above and below, then commands God's servants فَٱتَّقُونِ.
terra: The section contrasts revealing light with a heart-covering obstruction; this ayah sets a breast opened to submission and light against hearts hardened from God's remembrance.
terra: The section gives و ق ي the force of guarding a soul from what harms it; this prayer asks God to protect the faithful from evil deeds and says such protection on that Day is mercy.

luna: Night is for rest and day is made “مُبْصِرًا”; this repeats the section's specific cover-and-seeing pair. | terra: The section gives covering night and visible day complementary roles; this ayah makes night for rest and day for sight, though it does not stage their exchange.

luna: Thamud prefer blindness to guidance and are seized by humiliating punishment; this directly connects the section's opening/covering imagery to its moral and Thamud ending. | terra: The section turns daylight and darkness into moral sight and blindness; this ayah says Thamud preferred blindness to guidance and was seized by a humiliating thunderbolt.

luna: After Thamud choose blindness and are punished in 41:17, this verse says the believers who feared God were saved; it makes the opposed outcomes explicit. | terra: The section reads Thamud's blindness against protective taqwā; immediately after their punishment, this ayah says God saved those who believed and practiced taqwā.
terra: The section's four opening oath-objects form one governed scene; this ayah names night, day, sun, and moon together and redirects worship from them to their Creator.
terra: The section's cloud over the sun's eye and its punishment-cover meet in this command to watch for the sky bringing a manifest smoke; 44:11 supplies that smoke's action on people.
terra: The section defines a collective punishment by its enveloping action; this ayah says the manifest smoke of 44:10 يَغْشَى ٱلنَّاسَ and identifies it as painful punishment.

luna: The alternation of night and day is one of God's signs, directly naming the cycle that the section stages through sun, moon, day, and night. | terra: The section's recurring cover and disclosure belongs to a system of signs; this ayah places the alternation of night and day among signs for a people who understand.
terra: The section's غِشَاوَة is an inward veil that prevents sight; this ayah places a veil over the sight of one whose desire has become his god, alongside sealed hearing and heart.

terra: The section's secondary عقر image is a cloud that covers the sun, while its coverings may protect or punish; this ayah turns a cloud people welcome as rain into the wind bearing the punishment they hastened.
terra: The section contrasts an eye-opening sign with stubborn rejection; this ayah says Thamud defied their Lord's command and the thunderbolt seized them while they were looking.
terra: The section's eradication leaves no remainder or escape; after the visible seizure in 51:44, this ayah says Thamud could neither rise nor obtain help.
luna: The heaven is built and expanded, a close parallel to the whole surah's invocation of heaven and what built it.

luna: The earth is spread out (“فَرَشْنَاهَا”); this gives a direct earth-expanse counterpart to the source section's spread/raised root branch. | terra: The section moves from the ordered sky to the earth spread out; this ayah says God spread the earth and praises the act of preparing it.
terra: The section defines taqwā through concrete protection; this ayah says God favored the people of Paradise and protected them, وَوَقَىٰنَا, from the scorching punishment.

terra: The section makes purification and taqwā determine the soul's fate; this ayah forbids declaring one's own soul pure and says God best knows who has taqwā, setting a boundary on self-purification.

luna: Thamud are named and “nothing was left”; this is the section's explicit parallel for annihilation after the camel episode. | terra: The section explains دمدمة as complete eradication of Thamud; this ayah states the corresponding result tersely: Thamud was left with nothing surviving.
luna: The preceding reference identifies the overthrown cities that 53:54 then says were covered; it fixes the referent of that covering image.

luna: The verse says “فَغَشَّاهَا مَا غَشَّىٰ”; the source-section root غ ش و again makes destruction a covering action, here over the overthrown cities of 53:53. | terra: The section links covering to collective destruction; in the same catalogue of destroyed peoples, this ayah describes the overturned city with the emphatic فَغَشَّىٰهَا مَا غَشَّىٰ.
terra: The section's moon grows complete within a measured order; this ayah presents the moon split as an eschatological sign, a direct reversal of lunar wholeness.

luna: The earth is made to gush springs (“فَجَّرْنَا الْأَرْضَ عُيُونًا”); this gives the source-section's split/opening root a second physical scene. | terra: The section develops ف ج ر as a splitting that may reveal light or tear a moral veil; this ayah uses the root for earth bursting into springs whose waters join the flood, a destructive physical opening.

luna: The she-camel is sent as a trial; the verse makes explicit the sign's testing role in the Thamud scene. | terra: The section treats the she-camel as a sight-opening test-sign; this ayah says she is sent as a trial and orders watchful patience.
luna: The water is apportioned between the people; this develops the provision and assigned turn around the camel.

luna: Their companion is summoned and hamstrings the camel, matching the source-section's root ع ق ر and its singular act of violence. | terra: The section says Thamud's most wretched man arose and hamstrung the camel; this ayah likewise has them summon their companion, who undertakes the act and عَقَرَ.
luna: The verse asks how God's punishment and warnings were, directly framing the consequence of the act in 54:29.

luna: A single blast leaves them like dry fence trimmings; the image gives a concrete form to the section's account of destruction and leveling. | terra: The section glosses دمدمة as uprooting without remainder; this ayah completes 54:29 with one blast reducing the people to dry, crushed enclosure material.

luna: Sun and moon are said to move by a calculation; this directly sharpens the section's image of their measured order. | terra: The section's light spreads by measured stages; this ayah states that sun and moon proceed بِحُسْبَانٍ, by precise reckoning.
luna: The Lord of the two easts and two wests frames the repeated rising and setting boundaries that the section's changing light makes perceptible.

luna: Night entering day and day entering night repeats the section's exchange of covering and opening as an ongoing sign. | terra: The section makes day and night exchange the same illuminated face; this ayah states their mutual entry and then turns to God's knowledge of what hearts contain.
terra: The section defines و ق ي through a covering that protects; this ayah uses the root in its concrete moral force, قُوا أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ نَارًا, protect selves and families from fire.
luna: Thamud and Ad deny the overwhelming event; this places Thamud's end among the judgment scenes developed in the section.

luna: Thamud are destroyed by the overwhelming blast (“الطَّاغِيَةِ”), a direct parallel to the section's destruction and annihilation language. | terra: The section attributes Thamud's denial to طَغْوَىٰ and its end to eradication; this ayah says Thamud were destroyed by the overwhelming transgression or blast, ٱلطَّاغِيَةِ.
luna: After the destruction account, the passage asks whether any remnant can be seen; it completes the no-remnant aspect also stated in 53:51.

luna: Noah's people cover themselves with garments while refusing to hear; the source-section covering root links bodily concealment with refusal of what is made clear. | terra: The section's covering can become chosen resistance to a sign; this ayah says Noah's people covered themselves with their garments and persisted in refusal.

luna: The verse distinguishes moonlight, “نُورًا,” from the sun as “سِرَاجًا,” giving the section's two bodies and the sun's emitted light separate roles. | terra: The section distinguishes the sun's emitted light from the following moon; this ayah likewise calls the moon a light and the sun a lamp.
terra: The section's طَحَىٰهَا names the earth laid out beneath the sky; this ayah says God made the earth an expanse for people.
terra: The section follows the moon within a coordinated sequence; this ayah opens another three-part celestial oath with the moon, continued by retreating night and revealing morning in 74:33-34.

luna: Night as it departs (“إِذَا أَدْبَرَ”) continues the section's sequence from cover toward opening. | terra: The section's night belongs to a relay rather than a static darkness; this ayah swears by night as it turns away, between the moon of 74:32 and morning of 74:34.

luna: Dawn as it brightens (“إِذَا أَسْفَرَ”) supplies the light-revealing counterpart to 74:33 and the section's day scene. | terra: The section describes dawn as night's covering being opened; this ayah completes the neighbouring sequence with morning when it shines clearly.
luna: The oath by the self-reproaching soul names inward moral reckoning, giving the section's nafs a distinct ethical voice.
luna: The verse describes a person wanting to persist in fujur; it uses the source-section's moral root for deliberate wrongdoing.

luna: The resurrection scene begins with sight being dazzled; it marks a boundary to the section's stable, visible celestial order. | terra: The section depends on disclosure producing sight; this ayah contributes dazzled vision at the opening of the sequence whose moon is darkened in 75:8 and whose sun and moon are joined in 75:9.

luna: The moon is eclipsed, reversing its ordered following and fullness in the section's sky image. | terra: The section's moon participates in a luminous, measured order; this ayah's moon is darkened at the last upheaval, a direct boundary to that order.

luna: The sun and moon are brought together, a direct reversal of their ordered separation in 36:40 and the section's successive sky roles. | terra: The section depends on sun and moon keeping their respective places; this ayah gathers sun and moon together in the eschatological collapse of that arrangement.
terra: The section's opened or darkened face makes an inward condition visible; this ayah presents faces on that Day as radiant, before giving the opposite faces in 75:24.
terra: The section moves covering and darkness from the sky to moral fate; this ayah contributes the gloomy faces opposite the radiant ones of 75:22.
terra: The section's fashioned soul stands within a measured created order; this ayah says God created the developing human and سَوَّىٰ, proportioned him.
luna: The human is shown the way and may be grateful or ungrateful; it gives another explicit formulation of moral choice corresponding to fujur and taqwa.

luna: God protects the righteous from that day's evil and gives them radiance and joy; this connects the source-section's protective sense of و ق ي with its light imagery. | terra: The section joins protection to light appearing on a face; this ayah says God protected them from that Day's evil and met them with radiance and joy.
terra: The section's secondary ضحى sense is exposure to the sun and its coverings may protect; this ayah depicts Paradise as a place where its people see neither oppressive sun nor bitter cold.
terra: The section's spread earth is made fit beneath the alternating sky; this ayah describes earth as a resting place, a functional parallel rather than the same spreading action.

luna: Night as “لِبَاسًا” gives a direct garment image for the source-section's covering action. | terra: The section's night is a covering that belongs to created order; this ayah makes night itself a garment.

luna: Day is appointed “مَعَاشًا” after night as garment in 78:10, completing the cover-and-open pair with a distinct daytime role. | terra: The section's day opens what night covers; following night-as-garment in 78:10, this ayah makes day the time of livelihood.

luna: The sun is called “سِرَاجًا وَهَّاجًا,” a blazing lamp, matching the source section's sun as a source of spreading light. | terra: The section calls the sun a source that spreads its own light; this ayah names the sun a blazing lamp.

terra: The section makes purification the alternative to burying the soul; Moses' invitation to Pharaoh, هَل لَّكَ إِلَىٰٓ أَن تَزَكَّىٰ, turns that possibility into a direct call to one headed toward ruin.

luna: This is the question about whether people or heaven is harder to create; it supplies the creation context that 79:29 continues with night and ḍuḥā. | terra: The section carries meanings from the built sky into the fashioned soul; this ayah frames 79:28-30 by asking resurrection-deniers whether their creation or heaven's is harder.

luna: The heaven is raised and proportioned (“فَسَوَّاهَا”), completing the sky-building context before 79:29 turns to its night and morning. | terra: The section hears lunar completion in س و ي and places the fashioned soul under the built sky; this ayah says God raised heaven's canopy and سَوَّىٰهَا immediately before darkening its night.

luna: Night is darkened and its ḍuḥā is brought forth; the passage renders the section's opening and covering as a single created transition. | terra: The section says dawn-light is drawn out of night; this ayah directly pairs darkening the sky's night with bringing out its ضُحَىٰ.

luna: After the 79:27–29 sky scene, the earth is spread (“دَحَاهَا”) with a different root from source-section ط ح و; the shared feature is the created expanse, not a shared root. | terra: The section moves from the sky's night and forenoon to the earth spread beneath it; this ayah continues 79:29 with the earth being spread out.

luna: The verse uses ḍuḥā as a portion of the day that seems brief at the resurrection; it extends the section's measured morning interval into a perspective on time's passing. | terra: The section measures expanding daylight in named stages; this ayah compresses worldly duration to an evening or its ضُحَىٰ, using the two ends as a measure of passing time.
luna: The verse asks whether the listener may purify himself; the root ز ك و directly parallels the section's self-purification.
luna: The next verse adds taking heed, completing 80:3's possibility of purification with a response to reminder.
terra: The section uses visible brightness as disclosure of an inner state; this ayah presents faces on that Day as bright and shining.
terra: The section's one visible face can be covered rather than opened; this ayah puts dust upon other faces, beginning the reverse of the bright faces in 80:38.
terra: The section's covering produces darkness over a face; this ayah adds a dark pall over the dust-covered faces of 80:40.

luna: At the world's ending the sun is folded up, a direct reversal of the section's sun as a source whose light spreads. | terra: The section's sun spreads its own brightness; this ayah begins the last-day reversal with the sun folded up and darkened.

luna: The next scene turns to a girl buried alive; it begins the buried-child image that 81:9 completes and that parallels the section's account of hiding a daughter in earth. | terra: The section invokes the contemplated burial of a daughter to illuminate burying the soul; this ayah brings the girl actually buried alive into judgment and lets her be questioned.

luna: The buried girl is asked for what sin she was killed; this gives the section's concealment/burial image its moral consequence. | terra: The section exposes the guilt hidden beneath burial; this ayah asks the buried girl for what sin she was killed, completing the disclosure begun in 81:8.
luna: The preceding oath turns to retreating stars before the departing night and breathing dawn of 81:17–18; it extends that passage's transition from covered sky to morning.
luna: The next description says these stars move and disappear, continuing 81:15's retreating-star scene before the night and dawn of 81:17–18.

luna: Night as it recedes (“عَسْعَسَ”) supplies another exact transition from darkness toward the breathing dawn in 81:18. | terra: The section treats night and breathing dawn as successive movements; this ayah's night إِذَا عَسْعَسَ, whether advancing or receding, is the immediate counterpart to the dawn that breathes in 81:18.

luna: The source-section root ن ف س is linked to breathing; here dawn “تَنَفَّسَ,” giving that dictionary branch a direct Quranic morning scene. | terra: The section hears the root of نَفْس in dawn's breathing; this ayah supplies the exact celestial image, وَٱلصُّبْحِ إِذَا تَنَفَّسَ.
terra: The section begins under a built and ordered heaven; this ayah opens an opposite sequence with heaven split apart, followed by scattered stars and burst seas in 82:2-3.
terra: The section's celestial bodies keep their allotted order; this ayah contributes the stars scattering between heaven's rupture in 82:1 and the seas' rupture in 82:3.
terra: The section contrasts the ordered split of dawn with fujūr as a ruinous tearing; this ayah uses the same ف ج ر family for seas bursting open in the world's final disorder.
terra: The section hears completeness in the family of س و ي and applies the same verb to the soul; this ayah tells the human that God created, fashioned, and proportioned him.

luna: The righteous are in bliss, immediately before 82:14 names the wicked; this supplies one side of the moral polarity represented by the section's taqwa and fujur. | terra: The section places the soul's guarded and ruptured possibilities side by side; this ayah supplies the righteous side of the immediate pair, in bliss opposite the fujjār of 82:14.

luna: The wicked (“الْفُجَّارَ”) are in the fire, directly using the source-section's f-j-r moral branch as the counterpart to 82:13's righteous. | terra: The section defines fujūr as tearing the protective religious veil; this ayah gives the fujjār their corresponding destination in the Blaze, opposite the righteous of 82:13.
luna: The record of the wicked is named with “الْفُجَّارِ”; this is another direct Quranic use of the source-section's moral root.
terra: The section glosses the inward غشاوة as rust that covers a heart; this ayah names that very obstruction as the رَانَ accumulated by people's deeds upon their hearts.

luna: The oath by “الشَّفَقِ” places the fading twilight boundary between daylight and the night-cover developed in the section. | terra: The section tracks measured transitions of one light-bearing sky; this oath by twilight begins the sequence that moves through gathering night to the full moon in 84:17-18.

luna: Night and what it gathers (“وَاللَّيْلِ وَمَا وَسَقَ”) gives the covering half of the scene an explicit collecting action. | terra: The section's night covers and gathers the visible world; this ayah swears by night and what it وَسَقَ, directly preceding the full moon of 84:18.

luna: The oath by the moon when it is full (“إِذَا اتَّسَقَ”) matches the source-section dictionary branch linking س و ي with the moon at fullness. | terra: The section finds in the family of س و ي the night when the moon becomes complete; this ayah swears by the moon إِذَا ٱتَّسَقَ, when it grows full.

luna: On the day hidden things are exposed (“السَّرَائِرُ”), the section's movement from visible light to self-concealment is reversed into disclosure. | terra: The section's failed soul is hidden and buried while daylight discloses; this ayah names the day when inward secrets are tested and exposed.
terra: The section's سَوَّىٰهَا is a making-fit that echoes celestial completion; this ayah gives the same sequence in general form: God created and proportioned.

luna: The verse says “قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكَّىٰ,” closely matching the source section's claim that one who purifies the self succeeds. | terra: The section states that the one who grows and purifies the soul succeeds; this ayah repeats the compact formula قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ.
luna: The next verse joins remembrance of the Lord's name with prayer to the purification in 87:14, completing that account of successful self-cultivation.

luna: The name “الْغَاشِيَةِ” uses the source-section covering root for an overwhelming event, extending the cover image to judgment. | terra: The section develops غَاشِيَة as a punishment named by its enveloping action; this ayah names the coming overwhelming event itself ٱلْغَاشِيَةُ.

luna: The verse asks how the earth was spread (“سُطِحَتْ”), paralleling the source-section's secondary raised/spread dictionary sense for the 91:6 root ط ح و. | terra: The section includes the earth spread beneath its celestial scene; this ayah asks the reader to look at the earth and how it was spread flat.

luna: The oath by dawn uses the source-section's root ف ج ر for daybreak, the light that breaks into the night in the section's dictionary image. | terra: The section defines فجر as the redness that splits night's blackness; this ayah makes that splitting dawn an oath.
terra: The section ends its celestial vocabulary with succession; this ayah swears by night as it journeys away, making departure part of the nightly turn.
luna: Thamud are recalled as those who carved rock in the valley; this locates the people from the section's closing episode in another account of their history.
luna: God guides the human being to the two ways (“النَّجْدَيْنِ”); this states the moral alternatives that the section locates within the self.
terra: The section's destructive covering becomes total enclosure; this ayah likewise places a fire closed over the people of the left.

luna: The verse's “إِذَا يَغْشَىٰ” makes night cover the scene, directly repeating the source-section covering verb and its sky role. | terra: This repeats the section's exact night action, وَٱلَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَىٰ, making covering itself the object of the adjacent surah's oath.

luna: The verse's “إِذَا تَجَلَّىٰ” sets the day opening into view against the night that covers in 92:1, matching the section's paired actions. | terra: The section's day uncovers the sun through the root ج ل و; this ayah swears by day when it تَجَلَّىٰ, the luminous counterpart to the preceding covering night.

terra: After the same covering night and revealing day of 92:1-2, this ayah states that human striving is diverse, echoing the section's move from the divided sky scene to the soul's two possibilities.

luna: The person who gives and is mindful supplies a concrete moral counterpart to the section's taqwa as the soul's protective orientation. | terra: The section places taqwā on the protecting side of the soul's division; after 92:4 announces divergent striving, this ayah begins one path with giving and having taqwā.
terra: The section's inward alternatives become enacted choices; this ayah adds affirmation of the best promise to the giving and taqwā of 92:5 before their consequence in 92:7.

luna: The one who gives and is mindful is facilitated toward ease; this parallels the section's success for the soul cultivated in taqwa. | terra: The section binds the soul's protective choice to its outcome; this ayah contributes the result for the 92:5-6 path by promising facilitation toward ease.

luna: The opposite person withholds and considers himself self-sufficient, giving a specific moral contrast to the section's fujur and self-burying. | terra: The section's two inner possibilities issue in opposed paths; this ayah begins the reverse path with withholding and self-sufficiency, against 92:5's giving and taqwā.
terra: The section's moral rupture rejects what should guard the soul; this ayah adds denial of the best promise to 92:8's withholding before the result in 92:10.

luna: The withholding person's path is facilitated toward hardship; this makes explicit the failure-side outcome parallel to the section's contrast between purification and concealment. | terra: The section binds the destructive choice of the soul to failure; this ayah contributes the result for 92:8-9 by promising facilitation toward hardship.
luna: The most mindful is kept away from the Fire; this gives a concrete protective outcome to the section's account of taqwa.

luna: The person gives wealth to purify himself (“يَتَزَكَّىٰ”); this makes purification an enacted growth and cleansing, as in the source-section root ز ك و. | terra: The section says the soul succeeds by growing and purification rather than burial; this ayah describes the giver of wealth as seeking to purify himself.

luna: The oath “وَالضُّحَىٰ” directly names the opening section's spreading morning light. | terra: The section begins with the spreading brightness of ضُحَىٰ; this ayah makes that same forenoon brightness an oath.

luna: The oath by night when it settles sets the covered counterpart beside 93:1's ḍuḥā, preserving the section's paired scene. | terra: The section pairs spreading daylight with covering night; this ayah places night when it grows still beside the oath by forenoon in 93:1.
terra: The section makes burial the image of a soul forced from visibility; this ayah reverses concealment when what lies in graves is scattered out, before hearts are disclosed in 100:10.
terra: The section transfers opening and covering from sky to the inner self; this ayah contributes the bringing out of what breasts contain after graves are opened in 100:9.
terra: The section glosses دمدمة as a punishment closed down over its victims; this ayah describes the Fire as عَلَيْهِم مُّؤْصَدَةٌ, shut over them.
terra: The section's dawn is a rupture that releases light from darkness; this ayah names God as Lord of the daybreak, ٱلْفَلَقِ, using a different root for the same splitting scene.
